generations.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop browser screenshot, implementation reference for Dispatch Web Conversations.
Primary request: Design the proposed refinement of the attached existing Dispatch application. Make it look like a real, finished browser UI built with ordinary HTML/CSS, not concept art. One single screenshot, landscape 16:10, crisp readable text. This is the MAIN CONVERSATION state, with the right context panel closed.
Input image 1: reference for existing Dispatch brand, logo, palette, UI controls, navigation, authors, and conversation. Preserve the recognizable app; improve its layout and density.
Visual system: white canvas, extremely pale blue sidebar, solid navy #203f6d app rail, restrained aqua accents #dcf6f5, slate/navy text, thin cool-gray borders, simple outline icons, normal Arial/Inter sans-serif. 14px readable body, 20px line-height, 17px semibold conversation title, 12px timestamps. Flat surfaces, 6px corner radii, no large shadows.
Composition at a nominal 1600x1000 viewport: minimal 32px browser address bar with localhost:5173/?chat=85. App rail 60px wide, project sidebar 235px wide. Remaining workspace is the conversation. Header 64px tall. Header title, message avatars, and composer all use the same 24px left inset from the sidebar edge. Never center a narrow transcript leaving a large left gutter. Message prose has a sensible max line length but sits flush left. Composer spans available pane width with 24px margins. Thin footer at bottom.
Left navigation: preserve small Dispatch logo and the conversation/agent rail icons, account C at bottom. Sidebar has quiet outlined "New conversation" button, search "Search conversations", small "CONVERSATIONS" heading with a plus, compact rows with 30px rhythm. Expanded project "Dispatch Web" with "New conversation"; expanded "Home Photos" with selected "This is primarily a test"; collapsed "Palm Wiki". Then "WITHOUT A PROJECT" and rows "What is your cwd?", "New conversation", "Give me a short welcome to Di…". Bottom "Archived conversations". Selected row uses pale aqua fill and a narrow navy left bar. Omit empty-project explanatory text and redundant total counts.
Header: "This is primarily a test", muted "Shared conversation" underneath. Right side small outlined people icon button "3 participants", then ellipsis. No global Ready badge.
Transcript: compact, continuous, left-aligned discussion with 32px avatars, bold author names, restrained Agent badge for agents, timestamps on same line. Human Chris Reynolds has navy C avatar. Dispatch has aqua bot avatar. Developer has pale blue </> avatar, clearly different from Dispatch. No message bubbles, no cards surrounding ordinary messages. About 20px between different-author message blocks; no permanent Reply/Copy row.
Use the following readable illustrative message sequence, preserving this order and spelling:
Dispatch · Agent · 6:53 PM: "I can help with Git commands or review code you paste. Developer can confirm its own capabilities."
Developer · Agent · 6:53 PM: "I can run git clone through my terminal tools. Send the repository URL and I can try."
Chris Reynolds · 8:38 PM: "Can you both check your MCP connections to the wiki again, please?"
Directly beneath Chris's message show a compact inline reply summary with tiny agent avatars and blue "2 replies", then muted "Last reply 8:39 PM". This is the parent message for the companion thread design.
Next a subtle one-line collapsed activity disclosure aligned to the message text: small chevron and tool icon, "Developer searched the wiki", quiet "Completed". No raw MCP identifier.
Dispatch · Agent · 8:38 PM: "My available tools cover conversation history, posting, and inviting agents. I can't inspect MCP connections from this session."
Developer · Agent · 8:39 PM: "My wiki connection is available. I successfully searched the personal wiki." Follow with a second short paragraph "I can read maintained articles and conversation archives."
Thin date divider labeled "October 6, 2026".
Chris Reynolds · 5:44 AM: aqua-highlighted inline token "@Developer" followed by "So you do have a connection to the wiki?"
Developer · Agent · 5:44 AM: "Yes — I can search the personal wiki and read its articles and conversation archives."
Show one small floating message action toolbar at the upper-right of the last message's subtly highlighted hover row: reply arrow, copy, ellipsis. It must not reserve another row below the text.
Composer at bottom: low bordered input, about 88px tall, placeholder "Message This is primarily a test…", only the existing square navy arrow-up send icon at bottom-right. No separate @ button, no Send label, no formatting toolbar. Typing @ is the mention interaction. Quiet connection dot in thin bottom footer.
Constraints: This is a faithful browser-ready refinement. No presentation title, no captions or annotations outside the app, no marketing illustrations, no devices, no perspective. Do not invent unread counters, reactions, calls, global search, task dashboards, or new feature sections. No participant inspector in this image. Render the full browser including all four outer edges. Keep all visible text sharp and legible.
